title: Lordvessel
snippet:
Lordvessel -  Dark Souls - item - trivia 
 trivia : In *Dark Souls II*, shards of a shattered Lordvessel can be found scattered about the ground of the basin of the mansion in Majula. Another Lordvessel, whole and unbroken, is hidden underneath the map in the same mansion: it untimately wasn't used in the finished game, but it was meant to probably be obtained once again by the player.
The presence of the Lordvessel as the basin in which the Firelink Shrine's bonfire is placed and the broken one found in Majula (despite being, in this case, a less natural consequence than the first case) explain why, unlike in *Dark Souls*, the player can teleport between bonfires from the very beginning.

title: Lordvessel
snippet:
Lordvessel -  Dark Souls - item - notes 
 notes : It is possible to access the Kiln of the First Flame without interacting with either Frampt or Kaathe by dropping down the opening Frampt springs from. However, doing so before placing the Lordvessel will alienate the serpents and cause both of them to leave.
It is impossible to summon any phantoms at any of the Lord Boss' (excluding the Four Kings) locations without placing the Lordvessel with Frampt or Kaathe. Bloodstains, Messages and player ghosts will appear as usual and it is possible to be summoned, but not *to* summon.
To place the Lordvessel under the guidance of Kaathe, one must first continue on to the New Londo Ruins and defeat the Four Kings in order to gain access to him.

title: Lordvessel
snippet:
Lordvessel -  Dark Souls - item - general_information 
 general_information : Upon acquiring the Lordvessel, players can warp to select bonfires. Players must rest at a bonfire in order to use the warping ability. It is possible to warp from any bonfire, excluding the ones in the Painted World of Ariamis, The Duke's Archives, Prison Tower (though this bonfire can actually be warped from if you use it from *outside* the cell), and the Undead Burg. Extinguished bonfires can still be warped to.

Under the guidance of either Darkstalker Kaathe or Kingseeker Frampt, the player may place the Lordvessel at the Firelink Altar. In doing so, boss areas containing the Lord Souls and Bequeathed Lord Soul Shards will become accessible. Once the Lordvessel is satiated, the doors to the Kiln of the First Flame are made open, where they may finally face the Lord of Cinder. Players still have the ability to warp, even after placing the Lordvessel.

title: Darkwraith (covenant)
snippet:
As long as the player does not place the Lordvessel when Kaathe is present in Firelink Altar, Frampt will not leave, regardless of whether or not the player is a member of the Darkwraiths.
However, the next time the player approaches Frampt, he will unavoidably transport them to the Firelink Altar too and "force" them to place the Lordvessel for him. Using a Homeward Bone or similar methods, to escape the altar without placing the Lordvessel, will allow the player to benefit from both of Kaathe's and Frampt's services, while still being part of the Darkwraith covenant.
Placing the Lordvessel while under Frampt's care will not remove the player from the Darkwraith covenant, although Kaathe will leave forever the next time they approach him at the Abyss.

title: Londor
snippet:

 search_for_a_lord : Since their inception, the goal of Londor always remained to find their awaited Lord of Hollows who could overthrow the order of the old gods and inherit the First Flame, wresting it from its kiln, so that the Undead could assume "the true face of mankind". Determined to free mankind from the shackles of the Gods, the Sable Church of Londor studied the Dark Soul and the Darksign. The result of their research was the Dark Sigil, an artifact capable of overpowering the sigil of fire placed around the Dark Soul, allowing the darkness which had accumulated in the body to flow free again, unlocking the full potential of humans.  notes : When Frampt transports the player to the Firelink Altar after retrieving the Lordvessel, it is not necessary to place it. By using a Homeward Bone or the Homeward miracle, it is possible to exit and continue using Frampt's feeding service and at the same time interact with Kaathe and join the Darkwraiths. As long as the player does not place the Lordvessel, neither serpent will depart.
The player should avoid attacking Frampt (unless he is asleep) as it may result in him leaving for the rest of the playthrough. If this happens, the player loses access to his feeding service and must either place the Lordvessel with Kaathe or do it alone by dropping down the hole Frampt was in.
Dropping down to the Firelink Altar after acquiring the Lordvessel without his help will make Frampt leave, whether the player placed it or not.

title: Darkstalker Kaathe
snippet:
Darkstalker Kaathe -  Dark Souls - character - notes 
 notes : It is possible to join the Darkwraith Covenant without placing the Lordvessel and thus not alienate Kingseeker Frampt. After answering "Yes" to Darkstalker Kaathe's question and being transported to the Firelink Altar - do not place the Lordvessel. Instead, use a Homeward Bone or the Homeward miracle to exit. As long as one does not place the Lordvessel, neither serpent will depart. In this way, the player can be both part of the Darkwraith Covenant and use Frampt's "Feeding" service.
In an [http://soulslore.wikidot.com/das1-game-no-shokutaku interview], it is confirmed by Miyazaki that the Chosen Undead's ancestor, that Kaathe mentions, is the Furtive Pygmy.
Kaathe will depart if the Chosen Undead places the Lordvessel while Kaathe is not present.

title: Kingseeker Frampt
snippet:
Kingseeker Frampt -  Dark Souls - character - plot 
 plot : Kingseeker Frampt appears in Firelink Shrine after the player rings both Bells of Awakening. He instructs the player to go to Anor Londo and obtain the Lordvessel. After the player obtains the Lordvessel, Frampt transports them to the entrance of the Kiln of the First Flame, and instructs the player to place the Lordvessel to gain access to the Kiln, and to ultimately kill Gwyn and prolong the Age of Fire.

Should the player give the Lordvessel to Kaathe instead, Frampt will become irate and leave the player for the rest of the playthrough.

title: Great Chaos Fireball
snippet:
Great Chaos Fireball -  Dark Souls - spell - general_information 
 general_information : The player hurls a giant fireball, which does a large amount of damage on impact with a good area of effect, identical to Great Fireball. The fireball has a fire attack power of 3.0 times the Pyromancy Flame's magic adjust and the lava pool has a fire attack power of 2.0 times the Pyromancy Flame's magic adjust.

Contrary to what the name suggests, Great Chaos Fireball does not scale with the player's amount of humanity (like Chaos weapons do). It can only be improved by upgrading and ascending the Pyromancy Flame used to cast it.

title: Lost Sinner
snippet:
Lost Sinner -  Dark Souls II - boss - trivia 
 trivia : The original Japanese term used for "sinner" (罪人) does not possess any gender meaning to it, being instead neutral.
In the JP text Sweet Shalquoir says that she tried to create (生みだ) the First Flame rather than light it, which is more equivalent to what the Witch of Izalith tried to do.

title: Abyss
snippet:
Abyss -  Dark Souls - location - trivia 
 trivia : Due to what was observed from Artorias, the phrase "falling into the Abyss" does not actually constitute entering it, but rather the near infinite and unconscious darkness of it seeking out lifeforms.
**This likely means that Wolnir was very much alive when he fell, which explains how he was able to teach grave wardens his pyromancy, though what exactly it really was that actually caused his death is uncertain.

title: Darkwraith (covenant)
snippet:
Darkwraith (covenant) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - notes 
 notes : Dying as a red phantom will cause the player to lose souls and humanity, which are dropped as a bloodstain where the player loads out of the game into the other player's world. This does not cause the player to become hollowed. As long as players can easily reach their bloodstain, this means that invading other worlds becomes completely free, as long they have a Red Eye Orb.
Leaving the covenant in any way will cause the Red Eye Orb (but not Cracked Red Eye Orbs) to become unusable.
It is not necessary to place the Lordvessel for Kaathe in order to join the Darkwraiths. One can simply use a Homeward Bone, commit suicide or similar methods, to exit the Firelink Altar after being transported there by Kaathe.
As long as the player does not place the Lordvessel when Kaathe is present in Firelink Altar, Frampt will not leave, regardless of whether or not the player is a member of the Darkwraiths.

title: Miniboss
snippet:
Miniboss -  Dark Souls - enemy - lead 
 lead : A **miniboss** is an enemy in *Dark Souls* that does not respawn when the player character dies or rests at a bonfire. Unlike bosses, minibosses do not have their health bar displayed in the center of the screen, and do not have special music.

title: Starting Armor Sets
snippet:
Starting Armor Sets -  Dark Souls - armor - lead 
 lead : **Starting armor sets** are the armor sets that are worn by the starting classes in *Dark Souls*. All classes except the Deprived class have their own armor set. The armor sets can also be found later on in the game, the player does not have to start as a particular class to obtain the armor.

title: Unknown Talisman
snippet:
Unknown Talisman -  Dark Souls - weapon - overview 
 overview : It was cut from the final release of the game, it is unknown how the player would have obtained it.

Due to its nature as cut content, the Unknown Talisman is simply a texture in the game files. This means that even if the player modified their save file to obtain it, it would have no stats.

title: Invaders
snippet:
Invaders -  Dark Souls - mechanic - demon_ruins 
 demon_ruins : Kirk, Knight of Thorns: Invades on the ledge right before the Capra Demon congregation. May drop Barbed Straight Sword and/or Spiked Shield. Kirk does not invade here if the Lordvessel has not been placed yet.

title: Backstep
snippet:
During the backstep, from frame 11 to 14, the player has hyperarmor, i.e. infinite poise. That means, no matter what hits the player, they will not stumble and stay on their feet. For example, the player can backstep through the boulders in Sen's Fortress without being knocked down. Keep in mind that you will still take damage, since the hyperarmor frames do not grant invincibility. The backwards ninja flip does not have hyperarmor frames.
When inputing an attack directly after the backstep, the player will perform a running attack. This can be very useful in combat, by dodging an enemy's attack with the backstep, then striking back with a running attack.

title: Darksign
snippet:
Usage of the Darksign can, however, be occasionally advantageous. Since it does not cause previous bloodstains to disappear, it may be preferable to use it over dying if players are faced with a dangerous situation and do not wish to permanently replace their old, valuable bloodstain with a new and relatively worthless one. The Darksign can be used if a player is stuck through glitching or some accident that caused them to be trapped, and does not have Homeward or Homeward Bones at hand. Manual use of the Darksign also does not cause un-hollowed status to be forfeited the way death would, so it's viable to use it instead of homeward bone if the player has less than 500 souls.

The Darksign can also be used when being invaded, but also having a bloodstain to recover.

title: Ring of Knowledge
snippet:
Ring of Knowledge -  Dark Souls II - ring - effect 
 effect : The Ring of Knowledge grants +5 points to the Intelligence stat. Note that this does not work to obtain level requirements to talk to other characters.

title: Talisman
snippet:
Talisman -  Dark Souls - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Unless playing as the Cleric class, the standard talisman is the first talisman that players are able to obtain. It is worse than the other talismans (except the Thorolund Talisman at higher levels of Faith, which does not scale) in terms of faith scaling for miracle adjust, but it has a lower faith requirement.

title: Petrified Dragon Bone
snippet:
Petrified Dragon Bone -  Dark Souls II - item - videos 
 videos : [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ijh9vUbptOI This video] shows how to quickly get as much Twinkling Titanite and Petrified Dragon Bone as desired. The use of Yearn facilitates the process, though the *Crown of the Sunken King* DLC needs to be installed. This method does not work in since using a Bonfire Ascetic does not reset chest loot.

title: Painted World of Ariamis
snippet:
Painted World of Ariamis -  Dark Souls - location - notes 
 notes : After exiting the Painted World safely, casting Homeward or using a Homeward Bone will return the player to the bonfire in Anor Londo, near the Darkmoon Knightess, and not the bonfire within the Painted World.
Later warping to the Painted World via the use of the Lordvessel and then using Homeward or a Homeward Bone will cause the player to be taken to the last outside bonfire rested at, so long as one does not rest at the bonfire within the Painted World of Ariamis. This method only works if warping into the Painted World through the use of the Lordvessel and will therefore be impossible if entering for the first time.
The player can hear eerie ambiance in the graveyard, near the prison blocks in the area to the right of Phalanx from the bonfire.

title: Parry and Riposte
snippet: Additionally, it is possible to parry attacks with a shield that the player does not meet the requirements to use, although the timing window is much shorter.

title: Mounted Overseer
snippet:
Mounted Overseers are often encountered in poison-filled areas so close combat is not advised unless the player has a strong poison resistance. It is safer to dispatch them from a safe distance with ranged weapons.

Shooting the Overseer itself does the same amount of damage as it does to its Mount.

title: Rusted Coin (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Rusted Coin (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - item - notes 
 notes : Effect stacks with other items that boosts Item Discovery.
Using this coin along with the Symbol of Avarice, the Covetous Gold Serpent Ring +3, and the Crystal Sage's Rapier will increase Item Discovery up to 315 units.
Can be used on ladders.
Copper does not rust, though it does oxidize, becoming green or bluish green. This is very likely what is covering most of the coin.

title: Darksign
snippet:
Darksign -  Dark Souls II - item - general_information 
 general_information : Using the Darksign causes the player to return to the last Bonfire they rested at, but also causes the player to lose all humanity and souls on the person at the time.

Using the Darksign does not cause a bloodstain to appear; the souls and Humanity lost are permanent. Using the Darksign does not affect the previous bloodstain left by the player, which will still be available for reclamation.

title: Demon Firesage
snippet: The Chosen Undead encountered the Demon Firesage in the Demon Ruins, after they had placed the Lordvessel at the Firelink Altar, in their mission to destroy the Bed of Chaos and obtain the Lord Soul of Izalith contained within it. They proceeded to fight and slay the demon in combat thus gaining access to the ruins of Lost Izalith.

title: Oscar, Knight of Astora
snippet:
If the player answers "No" to his question (refusing to hear his tale and request), the only way to obtain the Estus Flask and the keys is to kill Oscar or rest at a bonfire. Despite being hurt by the player's refusal, Oscar still gracefully requests them to leave so that he does not hurt them after turning hollow.

Regardless of whether the player killed him in the first meeting or left him to die, Oscar is encountered again in the same area upon revisiting the Asylum, now a hollow enemy.

title: Corrosive Ant Queen
snippet:
Corrosive Ant Queen -  Dark Souls II - enemy - description 
 description : A gigantic ant found in a cave in The Gutter. She will spray a constant mist of corrosive acid which will degrade the durability of equipment over time. This mist will also cure poison.

The Queen is a stationary enemy and will not directly attack the player, apart from damaging their equipment, so it is advisable to use ranged weapons if the player does not wish to risk getting too close. She can also be assaulted from the back or front and does not react. She does not respawn.

title: Prowling Magus
snippet:
Prowling Magus -  Dark Souls II - enemy - notes 
 notes : The Magus encountered in the original game does not respawn.
The Magus encountered in *Scholar of the First Sin* does respawn.

title: Ringed City Pygmy
snippet:
Ringed City Pygmy -  Dark Souls III - character - plot 
 plot : The Ringed City Pygmy is the first character the player will meet when making their way past the Demon Prince. He doesn't have much of a purpose outside of pointing the player towards a new objective once they've finally reached the fabled city, which is to disturb Princess Filianore's slumber. He mainly serves an expository role.

He will disappear completely once the player does what he suggested and Filianore is awakened.

title: Arstor's Spear
snippet:
Arstor's Spear -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Upon killing an enemy with Arstor's Spear equipped, the wielder restores 30 HP. This effect is identical to the Ring of the Evil Eye, and can be stacked with it for additional healing per kill. It also shares all the same rules as the ring, which means that the player does not have to deliver the killing blow to get the heal, but the effect does not activate when hostile players die.

title: Abyss
snippet:
Abyss -  Dark Souls - location - characters 
 characters : Darkstalker Kaathe will appear after the boss has been defeated. The player cannot have placed the Lordvessel under Kingseeker Frampt's guidance yet; if they do so before having met Kaathe, Kaathe will not appear.

title: Black Knight Set (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Black Knight Set (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - armor - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Black Knight Set offers overall mediocre physical defenses for its weight. What it does have is decent Poise and very high Flame Defense, which ranks as the highest of any medium set when fully upgraded.

title: Intelligence (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Intelligence (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - notes 
 notes : The sorcery with the highest Intelligence requirement, White Dragon Breath, requires 50 Intelligence.
The Pyromancy Flame scales with Intelligence. However, the scaling does not increase adjustment for pyromancies, nor does it increase the damage the Pyromancy Flame deals with its Strong Attack.

title: Symbol of Avarice (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Symbol of Avarice (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - armor - how_to_obtain 
 how_to_obtain : The Symbol of Avarice is a potential drop from all Mimics encountered throughout the course of the game. It may even be obtained from the very first Mimic in the High Wall of Lothric. All Mimics have guaranteed drops, but they may also yield a Symbol of Avarice along with these.

Since Mimics are non-respawning enemies, each encounter with one is very valuable if one is looking to obtain a Symbol of Avarice. The player must first make sure their Item Discovery attribute is as high as possible. Crushing a Rusted Coin, or even a Rusted Gold Coin, before engaging a Mimic is recommended, as well as equipping the Covetous Gold Serpent Ring.

title: Darkwraith (covenant)
snippet:
Darkwraith (covenant) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - requirements 
 requirements : The player must place the Lordvessel for Kaathe instead of Frampt. The player could also speak to Kaathe and choose the "warp" option. After arriving at Firelink Altar, the player can then, instead of placing the Lordvessel, return to the Abyss and join the covenant while still keeping both serpents in the player's service.

title: Crimson Set
snippet:
Crimson Set -  Dark Souls - armor - plot 
 plot : The set is worn by Ingward and the other two sealers of New Londo, Yulva and one of Lautrec of Carim's unnamed companions, although said companion does not wear the head piece. The Mask of the Sealer symbolizes the resolve of the sealers to keep the seal shut and to demonstrate their atonement for those sacrificed in the process of sealing what is now the New Londo Ruins. The set that the player finds likely once belonged to Yulva, as her sorcery, Remedy, is found with it.

title: Wolnir's Crown
snippet:
Wolnir's Crown -  Dark Souls III - armor - notes 
 notes : Contrary to what one would expect from a unique boss armor piece, the crown does not grant any special abilities.

title: Darkwraith (covenant)
snippet:
Darkwraith (covenant) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : Accessing the Darkwraith covenant requires a few more steps than the others, as one must be able to speak with Kaathe. In order to access Kaathe, the Covenant of Artorias ring is required (obtained from killing the Great Grey Wolf Sif), as well as the Key to the Seal (obtained from Ingward) and defeating the Four Kings.

After defeating the Four Kings, Kaathe should appear if the player has not placed the Lordvessel for Frampt. Answering "Yes" to his question will make him transport the player to the Firelink Altar. Speaking to him again in the Abyss, after this event, will allow the player to join the Darkwraiths.

title: Xanthous Crown
snippet:
Xanthous Crown -  Dark Souls - armor - notes 
 notes : One Xanthous Crown per playthrough can be traded to Snuggly the Crow for a Ring of Favor and Protection. This is one of only two ways the player may obtain this ring.
Despite its large size, the Xanthous Crown does not impede movement through tight spaces in any way.
This item is a reference to the Monk's Head Collar from *Demon's Souls*.

title: Dragon Head Stone
snippet: Unlike most other covenant-related items, the Dragon Head Stone does not require membership of its parent covenant to use. Leaving the Path of the Dragon covenant does not affect usage of the head stone in any way, though the player will lose any covenant rank-dependent benefits (the increased fire damage from the head stone, as well as the increased buff power and roar range of the Dragon Torso Stone).

title: Gyrm Great Hammer
snippet:
Gyrm Great Hammer -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Gyrm Great Hammer is a strong great hammer. Compared to the Dragon Tooth that has the same weight, it has the same attack rating, but much shorter range and does not have the unique bonus defense. In fact, it is the shortest great hammer in the game.

What makes this great hammer useful is it's moveset, which helps dealing more Poise damage than many other great hammer.

title: Outcry
snippet: This spell does come with some downsides: the first and most obvious one is that is has a very limited amount of uses and requires two spell slots. Secondly, the spell has its own unique start up animation (the user's hand emitting dark flames before the cast is completed), meaning it can easily be distinguished from such spells as Fire Snake, thereby it cannot be used to keep an opponent player on edge as they know what is coming.

title: Mossfruit
snippet:
Mossfruit -  Dark Souls III - item - notes 
 notes : Despite the description, there is only one color of mossfruit available (pink), and it does not have the effect of moss (which cures build-up of effects, not raising the resistance of them, as mossfruit does).

title: Velka, the Goddess of Sin
snippet:
Velka, the Goddess of Sin -  Dark Souls III - character - services 
 services : ***Request Absolution**: The player can be cleansed of sin in exchange for souls equal to the player's Soul Level times 1,000.
***Request Dissolution**: The player can reset Hollowing buildup in exchange for souls equal to the player's Soul Level times 100. Does not remove Dark Sigils from the player's inventory and thus does not anger Yuria of Londor.
***Reinstate the King's Decree**: After defeating Halflight, Spear of the Church in *The Ringed City*, paying a fee equal to the player's Soul Level times 500 will revive Judicator Argo.

title: Cromwell the Pardoner
snippet:
Cromwell the Pardoner -  Dark Souls II - character - character_information 
 character_information : Cromwell, as his title implies, can be visited so the players may have their sins forgiven. This will remove the current sin title the player has, but it does allow hostile NPCs that the player provoked to become friendly again (the Royal Soldiers found in the Giant's Memories are excluded from this), as well as removing the damage penalty on the Lost Sinner's Sword, and thus reverting it to the normal damage it dealt.

He also sells many useful items, such as useful miracles (such as Great Heal and Perseverance) and the statusbite rings, which can greatly aid the player along the way.

He dons the Judgment Set, similarly to how Oswald of Carim donned the Black Set, and wields a Great Scythe.

title: Chaos Blade
snippet: The self-damage of Chaos Blade can be partially mitigated by equipping the Ring of the Evil Eye or by casting a heal-over-time Miracle like Replenishment. Chaos Blade does not damage its wielder if it does not hit anything. However, it still deals damage to its wielder if the player swings at an enemy during their dying animation. This is especially noticeable on large enemies with slow dying animations.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet:
Knight Artorias -  Dark Souls III - boss - trivia 
 trivia : Artorias's introduction cinematic is similar to that of the Penetrator in *Demon's Souls*, who impales a Fat Official and then tosses its corpse at the player.
Great Grey Wolf Sif wields the Greatsword of Artorias in the fight against the Chosen Undead.
Unusually for bosses, Artorias does not drop any form of Humanity. Other bosses that do not drop Humanity are Gwyndolin and Gwyn.
As *Berserk* happened to be among the favorite mangas of Hidetaka Miyazaki (the director of the *Dark Souls* franchise) and that he even approved how Catarina Set being based on Bazuso's armor, it's no surprise there are allusions to the aforementioned manga series in the game series proper. In Knight Artorias' case, he may very well influenced by Guts the Black Swordsman;

title: Royal Rat Authority
snippet:
#**Miracle** - The most essential miracle for the first part of the strategy is Lightning Spear. This is used to target each of the rats from across the arena and take them out before they can harm you or inflict you with Toxic buildup. In order to do this, one must first target the front left one. When the spear is thrown, do not wait to see if it kills the rat. Even with a low Faith stat, the base damage will kill them. If the player does not hesitate between throws, all the rats will be dead before the boss has a chance to attack. Alternatively, one can lure all the rats to them, and cast Soul Appease to defeat them instantly. This will damage the boss as well if you are in range.
#**Bow** - If your bow does over 200 damage, snipe the closest rat. Then lock onto the left-most rat and shoot. Before your arrow connects, shift to the next one to the right, shoot, and repeat for the rightmost rat. The Short Bow and Composite Bow work the best for this.

title: Spear of the Church
snippet:
Spear of the Church -  Dark Souls III - boss - strategy 
 strategy : Judicator Argo has a similar moveset to regular Judicator Giants, although he does not summon orange pact-bound spirits like them, and will only attack the player if they get close. Killing Argo has no benefits, as he drops nothing, only attacks the player if he gets close, and will perish on his own after some time. No matter what happens to him at the start of the battle, he will always reappear when the player is killed and retrys the fight, summoning the same three enemies again.

title: Falconer Set
snippet:
Falconer Set -  Dark Souls II - armor - characteristics 
 characteristics : Boasts overall balanced defenses and a moderate amount of poise for its low weight class, making it a suitable, and reliable, choice for many of the earlier parts of the game. The set does not shine in any aspect, it is just a reliable, and easily purchasable, armor set when the player starts out the game.

The chain mail concealed by the cloth tunic and the reinforced leather does, however, give it exceptional, and well-rounded, elemental defenses and a higher tolerance to strike attacks, notably more than the average metal armor set.

title: Resist Curse
snippet:
Resist Curse -  Dark Souls - spell - general_information 
 general_information : Resist Curse does not cure the effects of Curse, but only eliminates its buildup to prevent death. Despite the description, casting it does not reduce liquid Humanity.

title: Lingering Dragoncrest Ring
snippet:
Lingering Dragoncrest Ring -  Dark Souls - ring - notes 
 notes : While the Lingering Dragoncrest Ring increases the duration of the pyromancy Power Within, it does not increase the total damage Power Within deals to the player. The result is a slower decrease of HP for the player over a longer period of time, greatly increasing the practicality and usefulness of Power Within.

title: Bloodbite Ring
snippet:
Bloodbite Ring -  Dark Souls - ring - general_information 
 general_information : The Bloodbite Ring multiplies base Bleed resistance (via Endurance) by 4. The ring does not affect, nor it is affected by, resistance granted from armor. However, it does stack with weapons such as the Bloodshield, Gargoyle's Halberd and Gargoyle Tail Axe.

title: Way of White
snippet:
Way of White -  Dark Souls - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : Players may join the Way of White by talking either to Petrus at the Firelink Shrine or Reah after you have rescued her from the Tomb of the Giants.

Players who choose to be in the Knight class or the Cleric class begin the game already in the Way of White. (Though this does not unlock the trophy/achievement for discovering the Way of White covenant. Unlocking the trophy/achievement as a knight or cleric will require abandoning the covenant and then re-joining via talking to Petrus or Reah).

title: Giant's Kinship
snippet:
Giant's Kinship -  Dark Souls II - shield - trivia 
 trivia : Japanese translations reveal that the item's name is a mistranslation and that properly translates to "The Resonance With The Giants". It is not a physical item, but something the Bearer of the Curse gains from combating the Giants and the Giant Lord.
The original Japanese item description reads: "There is a throne fitting for each king. The view from the throne is known only to the one who sits upon it. Or does the throne show he who sits upon it what they want to see?".

title: Hawkeye Gough
snippet: Regardless of how Kalameet is defeated, Gough will reward the player with his personal greatbow, though he needs to be talked to for that to happen. The only way to obtain his set, however, is by slaying him, which can be done at any point. He'll drop the bow too if he hasn't gifted it already.

title: Old Knight Set
snippet:
Old Knight Set -  Dark Souls II - armor - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Old Knight Set offers an immense amount of Poise for how early it can be obtained. While it has high physical defence, bleed resistance and poise, its elemental defenses and other status resistances are underwhelming.

Like all Old Knight gear, the durability of the set is extremely low, requiring one to take preventive measures to ensure the set does not break prior to reaching the next bonfire.

title: Crestfallen Warrior
snippet:
Crestfallen Warrior -  Dark Souls - character - strategy 
 strategy : Players should avoid attacking the Crestfallen Warrior in the early game; he is very tough for a new player to kill and can offer helpful hints and tips. The Crestfallen Warrior is nimble with his Longsword and Heater Shield, but with some dodging and blocking he usually poses little threat by the time the player encounters him as a Hollow. The one trick up his sleeve is his ability to parry unexpectedly. The Crestfallen Warrior is one of the only NPCs that does not have a unique parry "stance", so players can do little to nothing to predict when he is going to do so.

title: Carhillion of the Fold
snippet:
Carhillion of the Fold -  Dark Souls II - character - equipment 
 equipment : Carhillion does wear leg armor. However it's a piece of clothing that players cannot obtain in any way. He also uses Dark Hail when summoned as a phantom, but he only uses it at close range.

title: Mimic (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
If a player attacks a normal chest, it won't display the amount of damage inflicted like an enemy. Be careful, though, as chests can be destroyed, turning its contents into Rubbish. If it's a Mimic, a health bar will appear, warning the player of danger. When a Mimic is hit, it won't do anything for a few seconds before it stands up and attacks.

When opening up, the Mimic can injure any player standing too close to it and, in cases with low Poise, will knock the player down. The Mimic uses a spitting attack that does decent damage, but is so poor to connect that it requires the player be almost directly in front of it. It can also attempt to grab the player but the animation is easy to spot and it has a short range.

title: Pilgrims of Dark
snippet:
Pilgrims of Dark -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : Players must talk to Darkdiver Grandahl in three separate locations:
#Shaded Woods: From the Shaded Ruins bonfire, advance forward until an open area is reached. Start walking right and past the two towers that lead to Scorpioness Najka. There will be a boarded up hole in the nearby grassy area by the cliff, which will let the player drop down to Grandahl. To break it, the player must simply walk over it.
#Black Gulch: Dropping down from the cliff near the two Razorback Nightcrawlers will land the player on a ledge with a locked door. To obtain the key for it, drop down two more times into an enclave that houses two Elite Giants; killing them will grant the Forgotten Key, along with a Soul of a Giant.

title: Poison Mist (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Poison Mist (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - spell - effect 
 effect : Produces a cloud of Poison, which can lead to the Poisoned status effect. The cloud does not harm the caster.

Poison and Toxic can be applied at the same time on the same target. They do not cancel each other out, but rather increase the rate of health degeneration.

title: Lightning Spear (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Lightning Spear (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - spell - general_information 
 general_information : Lightning Spear has a somewhat lengthy casting time and does not home in on targets the way Soul Spears do. It does, however, have a small AoE and will deal a small percentage of damage (10-15%) to nearby enemies. When cast at an enemy standing in water, Lightning Spear will do extra damage and have a noticeably larger AoE.

title: Heirs of the Sun
snippet:
Heirs of the Sun -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : To join the Heirs of the Sun, the player must simply reach the Altar of Sunlight, located in Harvest Valley, and interact with it. Joining the covenant will have the recieve the Sun Seal.

title: Salaman the Master Pyromancer
snippet:
Salaman the Master Pyromancer -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : Salaman's name is still shared by the Pyromancers of the Great Swamp, as well as the legends of his prodigious tutelage. title: Scythe
snippet:
Scythe -  Dark Souls - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Scythe is a more Dexterity-oriented Halberd, with standard base damage and higher dexterity scaling, but lower Strength scaling.

Like all Halberds, if the attack doesn't connect with an enemy, the user will stumble and seem to not be able to handle the weight. If the hit connects, the stumble animation does not come into play and the user moves as normal. This means that Scythe is capable of getting Sweet Spot Bonus Damage. Unlike most Halberds, Scythe does **** deal Thrust damage and does not get Counter Damage bonuses, making it and the other Scythe-named the weaker weapons within the Halberd class.

snippet:

Once the game has been reloaded or the player leaves Firelink Shrine, the visitors will be gone and Petrus will not talk much about what happened.

If the player talks to Lautrec of Carim he will offer information to the player for souls based upon level. He tells the player about how the lady and two companions went down to The Catacombs and got attacked, while Petrus escaped and left the others behind. If the player talks to Petrus after this, he will tell his side of the story and about how the lady is left alone and her companions have been turned to hollow.

Talking to Oswald of Carim will result in some implications and accusations against Petrus, claiming that his soul is drenched in sin.

title: Homeward (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Use of Homeward and other bonfire-warping items reset the area and all respawnable enemies, but it does not reset the character nor does it count as resting. Note that Estus Flasks and spell casts will not recharge as a result.

This spell, along with the Darksign, Aged Feather, and Homeward Bones will warp you back to the spawn gazebo in Things Betwixt if both the Fire Keeper's Dwelling in Things Betwixt and The Far Fire in Majula are unlit, potentially as a softlock prevention measure and/or a default warp location.

This is the only spell that will always have one cast, no matter what Attunement level the player is at. However, the use of items that grant extra casts, such as the Saint's Hood or a Northern Ritual Band variant, can be used to increase the number of spell casts.

title: Dragon Eye
snippet:
Dragon Eye -  Dark Souls - item - general_information 
 general_information : Usage of the Dragon Eye is limited to players who are members of the Path of the Dragon covenant.

Using the Dragon Eye causes the player's sign to appear in the worlds of other players, allowing them to summon the user to their world to duel. The player does not need to be in human form. However, the host must be in human form (reverse-hollowed), but does not need to possess a Dragon Scale (contrary to the in-game description), and the area boss does not need to be alive to interact with the summon sign; users of the dragon eye have no such restrictions as to where and when they can place their signs. title: Endurance (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Endurance (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - general_information 
 general_information : Increasing one's Endurance affects several attributes of the player. Endurance's main effect is to increase both the player's Stamina, as well as their total HP however, this does not increase it as much as raising Vigor will. Endurance is also interactive with Strength, Dexterity and Vitality, the sum of which determines the player's natural Physical Defense. Finally, Endurance is also interactive with the Adaptability stat, in that raising the two stats at the same rate will grant extra natural Poise.

Unlike in *Dark Souls* and *Demon's Souls*, raising Endurance does not improve a character's Equip Load.

Anor Londo (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - location - description 
 description : Unlike its Dark Souls counterpart, Anor Londo's illusionary shining sun is gone and has been replaced with the cold blue rays of the moon. The city has noticeably frozen over, as well as being severely reduced in size, with the only remaining parts of the old city being the cathedral, the rotating staircase, and the honorary tomb of Gwyn. An additional tower now stands where the entrance of the building housing the Painted World of Ariamis once stood, with an invisible walkway leading to the top. Additionally, only three of the Silver Knights remain and all Batwing Demons are gone. The cathedral has been overrun by Deacons of the Cathedral of the Deep and Writhing Rotten Flesh. The inside of the cathedral has been covered in corpses and maggots. The eastern section of the cathedral has been blocked off by debris, but the western section is still accessible and contains the body of an old blacksmith.

title: Anor Londo (Dark Souls III)
snippet: In the times of the kingdom of Lothric, things have changed. The beautiful city that once had a glowing sunlight is now cold and dark; the cathedral where the Chosen Undead once fought Ornstein and Smough is now corrupted by the Deep and the home to Gwyndolin, who took his father's title of King of the Gods but fell ill; and the chamber that once held Gwynevere now has nothing but the Sun Princess Ring. A denizen that came from the Painted World, Sulyvahn, infiltrated the city of Irithyll and Gwyndolin's Covenant and later proclaimed himself Pontiff. When Gwyndolin fell ill and became incapable of leading the city and the Covenant, he was forced to retire in the cathedral. The leadership passed to Captain Yorshka, Gwyndolin's crossbreed sister, who was immediately imprisoned by Sulyvahn. Sulyvahn converted Irithyll's knights to the worship of the Deep. The Pontiff then led his master and Saint of the Deep, Aldrich, to devour the helpless Gwyndolin.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet: Gwyndolin thus continued to remain hidden in his father's empty mausoleum, administering Anor Londo from the shadows and continuing to carry out his father's will to uphold the Age of Fire, punishing sinners and leading the Undead without revealing himself. At some point, he was visited by an Undead woman. The woman entered his service as a Blade of the Darkmoon and became the sole Fire Keeper in Anor Londo, although whether she was already a Keeper or became one upon entering his service is unclear. He gifted this "Darkmoon Knightess" with a golden armor set to hide her own "hideous form", as well as his Darkmoon special talisman and Darkmoon Blade miracle.  notes : Gwyndolin's corridor is not infinite and has a certain length. If he is forced to the end of the corridor, he won't be able to teleport anymore and will be at the player's mercy. He will attack relentlessly, trying to defend himself, but as his attacks are mostly designed for long range battle, just circling him will make most of them miss.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet:
Dark Sun Gwyndolin -  Dark Souls III - boss - strategies 
 strategies : Gwyndolin's boss battle takes place in a seemingly never-ending corridor.

He is not a very difficult boss if the player has decent dodging skills. Of his three attacks, two can be avoided by hiding behind pillars, while the last one is more powerful and fast (he will tend to use the Sphere Shot after Orb Spread if the player is hiding behind pillars). The main issue in this fight is reaching him, as he will teleport away when the player approaches (equipping the Ring of Fog may increase the time available to attack before he teleports), meaning that the best time to run up to him is when he is just finishing off his Arrow Spread, as he takes a few moments to recover. Gwyndolin can still be damaged while he is in his teleporting animation and for a split second after actually moving, so it is possible to deal considerable damage at that moment.
